note: Inline chat decisions (D-203 retired served rounds). Continues the D-NN sequence from round-6.

D-29.question: Which redesign direction does the site take?
D-29.context: He rejected the built design as too simplistic and lifted two constraints: the experience section no longer has to use the git-commit metaphor, and the site should look as good as a designer's portfolio, reversing his earlier framing. Four directions were built as standalone mockups and served locally for him to judge.

a-monograph.label: A, Monograph: editorial/publication register, Newsreader serif, numbered sections, bibliography
casesFor: Treats his output as literature, which is what it is
Ages best of the four
Craft lives in typography, not effects
casesAgainst: Closest of the four to the 'too simplistic' complaint he just made

b-instrument.label: B, Instrument: dark technical, field grid, rotating protein-ligand schematic, teal accent
casesFor: Reads as scientific software, so it says what he does immediately
Highest information density without feeling crowded
Teal identity survives intact on a dark ground
casesAgainst: Dark-only as built, so a light variant is a further decision
Dark technical is a common enough idiom to risk looking generic if executed loosely

c-bento.label: C, Bento: light tile grid, filled accent tile for the latest preprint
casesFor: Fastest of the four to scan
Serves the 'quickly get the information' goal best
casesAgainst: Least distinctive; bento is heavily used

d-kinetic.label: D, Kinetic: full-bleed teal field, Archivo at display scale, duotone portrait, keyword marquee
casesFor: Most likely to impress on first view
Boldest use of his teal
casesAgainst: Most likely to date
Spectacle competes with information

D-29.label: B, Instrument

supersedes.D-06: the git-log metaphor for the experience section
supersedes.D-14: the invented commit hashes, which go with the metaphor

opens: Light variant for a dark-first design (B is dark-only as built)
Typeface set: Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono, not yet ruled (supersedes D-16 if kept)
D-29.followUp: Four variations on B built for a second pass before anything is written into the Astro source.
D-29.retractionNote: He rejected direction B and every variation on it, along with A, C and D, and redirected to a blog-shaped site modelled on Hugo PaperMod (https://adityatelange.github.io/hugo-PaperMod/). The supersessions D-29 recorded do NOT revert: the git-log metaphor (D-06) and its invented hashes (D-14) stay dropped, and direction A 'Ledger' (D-17) stays superseded. Only the choice of B itself is void. Four PaperMod-idiom candidates built as P1 to P4.

D-30.question: How far does the retraction of D-29 reach? Does rejecting direction B reopen the git-log metaphor?
D-30.context: Claude wrote into the record that retracting D-29 voided only the choice of B while its supersessions survived. That scope was Claude's call, not his, so it was surfaced for confirmation. The metaphor was the previous site's signature element.

stays.label: No, it stays dropped. The record is already correct.
casesFor: The timeline reads as a timeline now, which is what he asked for
Keeps the design space narrow enough to converge
casesAgainst: Retires the one element the old site was recognised by

reopens.label: Yes, the metaphor is back on the table.
casesFor: He never ruled it permanently dead, only lifted the requirement to keep it
casesAgainst: Reopens a settled question and widens the search again

open.label: Neither. Leave it unresolved until a design is chosen.
casesFor: Defers a choice that the chosen design may make for him
casesAgainst: Leaves the record ambiguous while work continues

D-30.label: No, it stays dropped
D-30.confirms: The D-29 supersessions of D-06, D-14 and D-17 all stand.

D-31.question: Which blog-shaped design does the site take?
D-31.context: After rejecting directions A to D and the four B variations, he redirected to a blog-shaped site modelled on Hugo PaperMod. Four candidates were built in that idiom.

p1-paper.label: P1 Paper: faithful PaperMod, its own palette and system font stack, centred profile home, 720px column
casesFor: Closest to the reference he supplied
Cheapest path, since it is the theme rather than an interpretation
Restraint is the point of the idiom
casesAgainst: System font stack renders differently across platforms
No visual signature of his own

p2-type.label: P2 Type: same bones, Geist typography, left-aligned masthead
casesFor: Same structure with the typography actually chosen
casesAgainst: Departs from the reference for a gain he may not want

p3-index.label: P3 Index: archive-first, one reverse-chronological list with year gutter
casesFor: Reads full with only three publishable items
Solves where the CV lives
casesAgainst: Least like a conventional blog home

p4-sidebar.label: P4 Sidebar: persistent identity rail plus the same plain lists
casesFor: Handles four destinations better than a thin top nav
casesAgainst: A rail is not part of the PaperMod idiom

D-31.label: P1 Paper

supersedes.D-16: Inter everywhere, pending confirmation of the font stack

D-31.followUp: Four refinements of P1 built, each isolating one variable, before anything reaches the Astro source.
opens: D-03 (three pages: home with bio and timeline, Publications, Talks). A blog shape implies a different page set (home/posts index, post pages, publications, about, tags), but he ruled on a design, not on the page set. NOT superseded until he says so.
Theme toggle: PaperMod has one, it needs JavaScript, all candidates follow the system preference only.
Reading-time meta: omitted rather than invented; populates from real content.

D-32.question: Which refinement of P1 does the site take?
D-32.context: Four refinements of P1 were built, each isolating one variable: entry style (R1 Cards), home mode (R2 Direct), column width (R3 Wide) and typography (R4 Typed).

p1.label: P1 Paper, the unchanged baseline: system font stack, plain rows, 720px, full-viewport profile
casesFor: Stock PaperMod, no webfont request
casesAgainst: Renders differently on every platform, since the system stack resolves to SF, Segoe or something else

r1-cards.label: R1 Cards: PaperMod card entries on a tinted page
casesFor: Entries read as discrete objects
Also a stock PaperMod list style
casesAgainst: Needs a tinted page or cards vanish on white
Heavier than the plain list

r2-direct.label: R2 Direct: compact intro block, posts above the fold
casesFor: Puts content on screen immediately
Real usability gain, not a taste call
casesAgainst: Loses the full-viewport profile moment

r3-wide.label: R3 Wide: 1024px column with right-aligned per-entry meta
casesFor: More on screen at once
casesAgainst: Long measure hurts reading unless the width is spent on meta

r4-typed.label: R4 Typed: Manrope instead of the system stack, warmer ground, pill tags
casesFor: Renders identically for every visitor
Keeps P1's structure exactly, so only the type changes
Warmer ground and pill tags give it an identity of its own
casesAgainst: A webfont request
No longer stock PaperMod

D-32.label: R4 Typed

supersedes.D-16: Inter everywhere. Manrope carries every role now, and there is no monospace face.

inherits.D-28: Font delivery stays the Google Fonts CDN via a <link> plus preconnects, never a CSS @import and never self-hosted. That ruling was made for Inter and JetBrains Mono and is unchanged; only the font it applies to has changed.

D-33.question: Does choosing a blog-shaped design retire D-03, the three-page structure?
D-33.context: Claude had recorded D-31 as superseding D-03, then corrected it: he ruled on a design, not on a page set, so the supersession was an inference. Surfaced for a real answer.

retire.label: Yes, retire it. Take a blog page set: posts index, post pages, publications, about, tags.
casesFor: Matches the idiom the design comes from
casesAgainst: More pages to build and maintain for three items of content

keep.label: No, keep the three pages, rendered in the PaperMod idiom.
casesFor: D-03's reasoning still holds: the bio makes a claim and the timeline is its evidence
Fewer pages suits the amount of content he actually has
casesAgainst: Slightly unusual for a blog-shaped site to have no posts index

later.label: Decide once a refinement is picked.
casesFor: The real page set may become obvious
casesAgainst: Blocks the Astro routes

D-33.label: No, keep the three pages
D-33.note: For now, per his wording. D-03 stands.

D-34.question: When the code and the design specification disagree, which one is wrong?
D-34.context: Claude wrote a precedence rule into CLAUDE.md without balloting it, then surfaced it. It has teeth: it decides which side gets edited when a mismatch is found.

spec.label: The spec wins. Code is corrected to match .claude/rules/website-design.md.
casesFor: Directly serves the reason he asked for the file: the design is kept across edits
A drifting value gets pulled back automatically instead of quietly becoming the new design
casesAgainst: A deliberate code change that was never written into the spec gets reverted

code.label: The code wins. The spec is descriptive and gets updated to match reality.
casesFor: Never reverts real work
casesAgainst: The spec stops being a guard and becomes a changelog, which is what he was trying to avoid

stop.label: Neither. A mismatch stops work and is surfaced to him.
casesFor: Safest, no silent edit in either direction
casesAgainst: Slowest; interrupts him for what is usually a typo

D-34.label: The spec wins

D-35.question: What do the navigation items read, now that the three-page set stands?
D-35.context: The R4 mockup's nav read 'Posts | Publications | About | Contact', but D-33 keeps three pages where the posts section is Talks and the bio lives on the home page.

talks.label: Talks | Publications | About | Contact. Replace 'Posts' with 'Talks', leave the rest.
casesFor: Names the real destination rather than a generic blog label
Minimal change from the mockup he approved
casesAgainst: 'About' points at an anchor on the home page rather than a page of its own

posts.label: Keep 'Posts' as the generic blog label.
casesFor: Conventional for the idiom
casesAgainst: Misleading: the section holds talk write-ups, not posts in general

D-35.label: Talks | Publications | About | Contact
D-35.note: About resolves to the bio anchor on the home page. Contact is a mailto.

D-36.question: Should the academic vs professional distinction return to the experience list?
D-36.context: The old list coloured academic entries amber and professional ones teal (D-05). The rebuild dropped it because the R4 spec permits one accent. Surfaced because the consequence was never put to him: nine entries now read as one flat list.

flat.label: No, leave it flat. One accent, one list, chronology is the only structure.
casesFor: Keeps the one-accent invariant intact
Simplest, and chronology already carries the story
casesAgainst: Degrees no longer look different from short internships

label.label: Yes, without a second colour: a text label or weight change per entry.
casesFor: Restores the distinction without amending the spec
casesAgainst: Adds a element to every row for a distinction the dates mostly imply

colour.label: Yes, with a second colour. Amber returns for academic entries.
casesFor: Closest to the previous site
casesAgainst: Requires amending the one-accent invariant

D-36.label: No, leave it flat

D-37.question: Should the degree documents stay linked from the site?
D-37.context: D-22 ruled the six PDFs published and linked from their timeline entry rather than left reachable but unlinked. He has since raised a privacy concern about sharing diplomas and a full MSc transcript online.

unlink.label: Remove the links, keep the files.
casesFor: Stops the site advertising them while he thinks it over
Fully reversible: the document data stays in experience.ts
casesAgainst: Does NOT stop the files being downloadable, since they remain in public/ and are copied into docs/

keep.label: Keep them linked, as D-22 ruled.
casesFor: Verifiable credentials are useful to an academic reader
casesAgainst: Publishes a full transcript he is not sure he wants public

D-37.label: Remove the links, keep the files
D-37.why: Still not sure how safe it is to share diplomas and documents online; wants to think about it separately, and will ask to restore them if he decides to.

supersedes.D-22: The publish-and-link ruling. The files are no longer linked from any page.

D-37.openRisk: Unlinking is not unpublishing. The PDFs remain in public/ and are copied into docs/, so they stay fetchable at their original URLs, which were live on the previous site. Surfaced to him separately.

D-38.question: How often should work in this repository be committed?
D-38.context: The project CLAUDE.md said 'commit only when asked', which left a whole rebuild sitting uncommitted in the working tree.

often.label: Commit every time a small amount of work is done. Never push.
casesFor: Restore points as work proceeds instead of one sprawling change
Publishing stays a separate, explicit act, so cadence costs nothing
casesAgainst: More commits to curate later, though he squashes locally if he wants

onask.label: Keep committing reactive, only when he asks.
casesFor: He controls the history exactly
casesAgainst: Large changes accumulate uncommitted, which is what just happened

D-38.label: Commit every time a small amount of work is done, never push
D-38.note: Supersedes the 'commit only when asked' line in CLAUDE.md. The never-push rule is UNCHANGED and absolute.

D-39.question: Does 'About' stay in the navigation menu?
D-39.context: D-35 set the menu to Talks | Publications | About | Contact, with About resolving to an anchor on the home page rather than a page of its own.

remove.label: Remove it. The bio lives on the home page and that is enough.
casesFor: An anchor masquerading as a destination is misleading
The site name already links home, where the bio is
casesAgainst: A visitor on /talks/ has no labelled route back to the bio

keep.label: Keep it as an anchor to the home page bio.
casesFor: Names the bio explicitly from any page
casesAgainst: Behaves differently from the other menu items

D-39.label: Remove About from the menu

amends.D-35: The menu is now Talks | Publications | Contact.

D-40.question: How should the header stop shifting horizontally between pages?
D-40.context: A scrolling page is 15px narrower than a short one, and the header is centred, so its contents moved by half that: measured at 200.5px on the home page against 208px on Talks. Claude implemented a fix before surfacing the choice, then surfaced it.

gutter.label: scrollbar-gutter: stable on html. Reserve the width everywhere.
casesFor: Cleanest expression of the intent
No visible scrollbar track on short pages
casesAgainst: Baseline only since December 2024, so older browsers still show the jump
Leaves a thin reserved strip on every short page

overflow.label: overflow-y: scroll on html. Always render the scrollbar track.
casesFor: Works in every browser ever shipped
casesAgainst: A permanently visible, non-functional scrollbar track reads as heavier

layout.label: Stop centring the header: full-bleed background with padded contents.
casesFor: No compatibility floor at all, since scrollbar width cannot move it
casesAgainst: Changes the layout the specification pins and moves away from PaperMod

D-40.label: scrollbar-gutter: stable
D-40.note: Already implemented when surfaced; this confirms it. Accepts that pre-2025 browsers keep the jump.

D-41.question: Does scroll-padding-top stay on html?
D-41.context: The 80px reserve exists to stop in-page anchors landing under a fixed header, but the R4 header is not sticky and scrolls away. Its only remaining effect was to push the skip link's jump to #content 80px lower than necessary. Carried over from the mockups.

remove.label: Remove it. Nothing on the page needs the reserve.
casesFor: The header is not fixed, so there is nothing to clear
The skip link lands flush at the top of main, which is correct for a skip link
casesAgainst: Would need reinstating if the header ever becomes sticky

keep.label: Keep it as insurance in case the header becomes sticky later.
casesFor: Costs nothing visible today
casesAgainst: A value in the specification that serves nothing invites confusion

D-41.label: Remove it
D-41.note: scroll-behavior: smooth stays; it still governs the skip link jump and he did not ask for it to go.

D-42.question: Where does the decision-ownership boundary sit for front-end work in this repository?
D-42.context: Claude had been surfacing implementation-level front-end choices one at a time: the CSS mechanism for a layout fix, browser-support tradeoffs, orphan cleanup, spec clauses forced by a build. He said these are details he does not care about and asked for them to be implemented on judgement instead. His global boundary is explicitly his to tune.

tune.label: Technical implementation detail is Claude's to decide. He specifies effects.
casesFor: He is not the audience for a scrollbar-gutter versus overflow-y argument
Surfacing everything made the gate noise rather than signal, which weakens it
He keeps every choice he could actually be asked to defend
casesAgainst: Risks Claude reading the delegation too widely and deciding things that are his

keep.label: Keep surfacing every choice with a defensible why.
casesFor: Maximally conservative
casesAgainst: He explicitly said this is not what he wants here

D-42.label: Technical implementation detail is Claude's; he specifies effects
D-42.why: These are all details I don't care about. I will focus mostly on the effects I want to see; for the details of that, implement what you think would work best.

claude_decides: spec clauses that only describe how an agreed design is realised
still_his: what the site says, all copy (D-26)
the visual design direction and register
what content exists and what is published
anything he could be asked to justify to a person
anything that changes an effect he would notice and did not ask for

D-42.note: This tunes the boundary for THIS repository's front-end work only. It does not touch the research-side gate, where methodology choices stay his.

D-43.question: Do the inline rulings stay in inline-decisions.json, or move into the round-file format?
D-43.context: Open since D-29 and asked twice without an answer. Settled under D-42, which makes record-keeping mechanics implementation detail rather than something he must rule on.

keep.label: Keep inline-decisions.json. The round files stay frozen as history.
casesFor: D-203 retired served rounds, so there is no def.json for a round-7 to describe
Both formats are greppable JSON carrying question, options, choice and why
Backfilling D-01 to D-28 would rewrite files the round program wrote

migrate.label: Backfill everything into one file.
casesFor: A single record to grep
casesAgainst: Most work, and it rewrites the historical artefacts for tidiness alone

D-43.label: Keep inline-decisions.json alongside the frozen round files
D-43.note: Decided by Claude under D-42, not ruled by him. Reversible at any time; say so and it migrates.

D-44.question: How long should Claude's chat output be, and how big should each iteration be?
D-44.context: Reports were running to many paragraphs per turn and iterations were large.

short.label: Shortest possible output, small and frequent iterations.
casesFor: Less to read before he can react
Small steps are cheaper to redirect when wrong
casesAgainst: More turns; a real problem gets one line instead of an explanation

full.label: Keep full reports.
casesFor: Everything stated once
casesAgainst: He said it is too much to read

D-44.label: Shortest possible output, small frequent iterations
D-44.why: So that I have as little as possible to read before we iterate. Smaller shorter but more frequent iterations, that's the way I want to work.
D-44.note: Applies to chat output only. The decision record, commit messages and the design spec stay as detailed as they need to be, since they are read on demand rather than every turn.

D-45.question: Should the site offer a theme toggle?
D-45.context: The site followed the operating system setting with no way to override it.

add.label: Add one.
casesFor: Lets someone on a dark laptop read the site in light
Choice persists
casesAgainst: Needs JavaScript

no.label: Keep system preference only.
casesFor: No JavaScript at all
casesAgainst: No way to override the system

D-45.label: Add a theme toggle
D-45.note: Text label rather than an icon, to match the all-text menu. Hidden entirely without JavaScript so no dead control is shown. Content stays readable with JS off, so D-07 holds.
